healthcareSystem: British Overseas Territory with a small public hospital (Princess Alexandra Hospital). Limited specialist services. Serious cases evacuated to nearby islands or the US.
qualityNotes: Princess Alexandra Hospital provides basic emergency and inpatient care. Limited specialist services — no MRI or advanced diagnostics on-island. Serious conditions require evacuation to St. Maarten, Puerto Rico, or the US. Private clinics handle routine tourist needs.
pharmacyHours: Pharmacies open 8:30am-5pm weekdays, limited Saturday hours. No 24-hour pharmacies.
pharmacyTips: Small number of pharmacies on the island. Hospital pharmacy is the most reliable source. Bring all medications you need — stock is limited and resupply can be slow.
prescriptionRules: Prescription required for most medications. UK and US prescriptions generally accepted. Very limited stock — bring your own supply.

restrictedMeds.name: Controlled substances
restrictedMeds.note: Carry a doctor's letter and original prescription. Keep in original packaging.

bringDocumentation: Carry a doctor's letter for all prescription medications. English documentation is standard. Keep medications in original labeled packaging. Bring a full supply for your entire trip.

travelInsurance.tips: Medical evacuation insurance is ESSENTIAL. Evacuation to Puerto Rico or the US mainland can cost $15,000-40,000+. Ensure coverage includes water sports and hurricane-related emergencies.

vaccinations.notes: No special vaccinations required. Dengue fever and chikungunya present — use insect repellent. No malaria risk in Anguilla.

waterNotes: Tap water is safe to drink. Anguilla relies on desalinated water and rainwater collection. Bottled water is widely available.
foodSafetyTips: Food safety standards are good, especially at resorts and established restaurants. Fresh seafood is excellent. Standard Caribbean food hygiene practices apply.
medicalTourismNote: Anguilla is not a medical tourism destination. For specialized care, residents travel to St. Maarten, Puerto Rico, or the US.
metaDescription: Health guide for Anguilla. Emergency 911, hospital info, pharmacy tips, dengue prevention, and medical evacuation insurance for this Caribbean island.

hospitals.name: Princess Alexandra Hospital
hospitals.notes: Only hospital on the island. Emergency department, basic inpatient care. Limited diagnostics. English is the official language.

hospitals.name: Hughes Medical Center
hospitals.notes: Private medical center. Good for routine tourist health needs. More comfortable than the public hospital.

dentalCare.availability: A few private dental practices on the island. Basic and emergency dental care available.
dentalCare.notes: Limited dental services. For complex work, travel to St. Maarten or Puerto Rico.
dentalCare.emergencyTip: Contact Princess Alexandra Hospital or a private dentist in The Valley for dental emergencies.

mentalHealth.crisisLine: No dedicated crisis line. Contact Princess Alexandra Hospital: +1-264-497-2551
mentalHealth.internationalLine: Crisis Text Line: text HELLO to 741741 (US-based, available via SMS)
mentalHealth.englishTherapists: Very limited mental health services on-island. English is the native language.
mentalHealth.notes: Mental health services are extremely limited. Consider telehealth options. The hospital has basic psychiatric services.

accessibilityInfo.overview: Accessibility infrastructure is limited on this small island.
accessibilityInfo.hospitalAccess: Princess Alexandra Hospital has basic wheelchair access.
accessibilityInfo.transport: No public transport system. Taxis are the main option. Roads are generally paved but not always accessible.
accessibilityInfo.tips: Contact resorts in advance about accessibility features. Beach access may be challenging. Bring all mobility equipment.

covidStatus.entryRequirements: No COVID testing or vaccination requirements for entry as of 2026.
covidStatus.testing: Limited testing available at Princess Alexandra Hospital.
covidStatus.notes: Standard health precautions apply. Bring rapid tests if concerned.

insuranceClaimProcess: Princess Alexandra Hospital requires upfront payment for non-residents. Obtain itemized receipts. Credit cards accepted at private clinics. Keep all documentation for insurance reimbursement.

commonCosts.note: USD widely accepted. Costs are moderate for the Caribbean. Payment expected upfront from tourists.

medicalEvacuation.note: Air ambulance to Puerto Rico or the US is the standard evacuation route. St. Maarten (15 min by air) has more advanced facilities for intermediate cases.

drugNameMap.note: Widely available. US and UK brands common.
Available but bring your own supply to be safe.
